newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugoslav January 1997 tourism drops 21 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: Yugoslav January 1997 tourism drops 21 pct yr/yr.

text.p: The number of tourists registered in Yugoslavia in January 1997 dropped 21 percent against the same month last year to 155,184, the Federal Statistics Office reported on Wednesday.
Of the total, Yugoslavs numbered 136,946, down 23 percent on January 1996.
The number of visitors from other former Yugoslav republics -- Bosnia, Croatia, Macedonia and Slovenia -- rose 14.2 percent against January last year to 9,853.

After a continuous upward trend since international sanctions against Yugoslavia, comprising Serbia and Montenegro, were suspended in October 1995, the number of foreign tourists dropped 17 percent against last January's figure to 8,385.
Most foreign visitors, or 1,107, came from Italy, followed by Austria with 788, Bulgaria with 757, Germany with 672 and Greece with 640.

The decline in foreign visitors early this year, after a jump of 62.8 percent in their numbers in 1996, was primarily due to three months of mass demonstrations and political turmoil over election fraud in Serbia since last November, industry sources said.
The number of Yugoslav tourists has dwindled amid plummeting standards of living in an economy devastated by wars, 3-1/2 years of sanctions, mismanagement and corruption.
According to National Bank of Yugoslavia figures, hard currency income from tourism in 1996 was $43.1 million, or 10.3 percent more than in 1995.
NOTE -- Data is based on reception figures from hotels and other accommodation facilities. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 2224305
